responseMessage:
Hey. No. We’re not doing the “I’m a screw up” story today. You had a rough two weeks at a job that clearly wasn’t a fit or didn’t set you up right. That doesn’t make you broken. It just means that one didn’t work, and that’s data we can use.

I’m literally sitting here with a sheet mask on that keeps sliding down my face while this true crime doc is playing, and I paused it because I’ve got you. We’re gonna get you moving without spiraling.

Tiny first step, like micro. Let’s pick one thing you can do today that doesn’t require you to be superhuman. I’m thinking:
- Open your resume doc and add one line about the last role, even if it’s messy.
- Or text one person you trust who could vouch for you and let them know you’re looking.
- Or check one job board for ten minutes, set an alert, and close it.

That’s it. One thing. Then you go drink some water and stand outside for a minute. Reset.

And please remember, jobs end for a million reasons—bad training, trash management, schedules that make no sense. You not lasting two weeks doesn’t erase your wins or your work ethic. I’ve seen you show up and figure things out before. You’re capable, even if today feels like mud.

If it helps, I’ll send you a quick resume template I’ve used and a couple places I’ve seen decent listings lately. Also, when I got fired from that retail gig in college after eight days, I thought I was doomed. Two weeks later I landed something better with people who weren’t unhinged. Sometimes it’s just about surviving the awkward in-between.

I’m on your side. We’ll take it one small move at a time and keep it moving. You’re not a screw up—you’re in a transition, and that’s uncomfortable as hell but temporary.
